## Summary

A build-vs-buy take on **agentic code review**, quoting Cherny's "I could not imagine being productive without Claude Code Review… catches almost every bug before it goes in" as the SaaS anchor — then arguing the other side: for the best cost/quality balance, **don't** use the SaaS codex/claude reviewers. Instead:

1. Create your own agent, **triggered by GitHub webhooks** on PR raised/updated events.
2. Give it **company and architecture context**. Any key… *(truncated at capture)*

## Why it matters

- **The interesting claim is economic, not technical.** Both sides agree agentic review is now table stakes (Cherny calls it his team's "secret sauce"). Craig's disagreement is purely about *who operates the reviewer*: SaaS convenience vs. a self-hosted webhook agent you feed your own context into. That's the same shape as every infra build-vs-buy — the differentiators are context injection and marginal cost, not capability.
- **Context is his actual argument.** Item 2 (company + architecture context) is where a self-hosted agent should beat a generic SaaS reviewer: review quality presumably comes from knowing *this* codebase's patterns, not from a smarter model. Note the symmetry with our own operation — our agents' edge is exactly the accumulated company context (relay rules, vault conventions) that no SaaS has.
- **Fits the review-pipeline family.** [[2026-09-01-quentin-cody-code-quality-gates]] is prevention (gates against AI slop); [[2026-09-06-pocock-reviewable-ai-prs]] is how to keep AI PRs human-reviewable; [[2026-10-11-copyconstruct-debugging-agents-unreadable-code]] is diagnosis when review fails. This note is the *reviewer-selection* layer — who/what performs the review at what cost.
- **Skepticism gates:** the recipe is **truncated at item 2** — the concrete setup (model choice, context format, cost figures) is unseen, so nothing here is actionable yet. "Best balance between cost and quality" is asserted with **no numbers** on either side; Cherny's quote is enthusiasm, not measurement; n=0 evidence in-text.
